info.title: MozgoBolt API
info.description:
Backend API for MozgoBolt — real-time GPS tracking for mobile vendors (e.g. moving food trucks/bakeries) so buyers can see nearby vendor vehicles on a live map, ping a vehicle they're interested in, and get notified when a favorited company's vehicle enters an area they've saved.

Domain model: a vendor's first company creation makes them its admin; other vendors join via invite code. A company owns vehicles; a vendor links themself to a vehicle for a driving session (an active `VehicleAssignment`) and unlinks at the end of it — all GPS telemetry is tied to whichever vehicle currently has an active assignment for the calling vendor, never directly to the vendor. A buyer favorites companies (not individual vehicles) and can save named locations to be notified about.

Rate limits: a global 150 requests/minute per client; every `/api/v1/auth/*` endpoint additionally enforces 5 requests/minute (429); every other authenticated endpoint enforces 60 requests/minute keyed by user id (429); file-upload endpoints enforce a stricter 10 requests/minute. POST/PATCH bodies are size-limited (413 when exceeded) and requests time out server-side (504). Error bodies, where present, use the `ErrorResponse` shape; `error` is the machine-readable code to switch on, `message`/`details` are human-readable context only.

Two endpoints are Server-Sent Events (SSE) streams, not typical request/response — `GET /vehicle-tracking/live` and `GET /vehicle-tracking/pings/live` — documented below with the event types each one emits, since OpenAPI has no first-class SSE modeling.

latitude.description: Privacy-coarsened to an H3 cell center, never the buyer's exact position

longitude.description: Privacy-coarsened to an H3 cell center, never the buyer's exact position

patch.description: Full-replace, not a partial patch — the client always sends every field's current desired state. Setting a field to `null` removes it entirely; setting its matching `*Visible` flag to `false` hides an already-set value from buyers without deleting it (independent controls). `phoneNumber` validates as Hungary-only; `whatsappNumber`/`viberNumber` validate as any valid international number.

Idempotent: re-linking to the vehicle you're already on is a clean success. Rejected for an archived vehicle.

post.description: Vendor-only. Tied to the caller's currently active vehicle assignment — there is no vehicle id parameter; the backend resolves it server-side, so a vendor cannot report telemetry for a vehicle they're not driving. Points implausible relative to the previous accepted point (e.g. faster than 200 km/h, allowing ~500m of GPS jitter for ambiguously-ordered timestamps) are silently dropped, not rejected. Max 100 points per batch.

202.description: Accepted (points may have been individually dropped as implausible)

409.description: Caller has no active vehicle assignment

get.description:
Server-Sent Events stream. Any authenticated user. Query params: `scope` (`nearby`, the default, or `all` — the explicit opt-in "see everything nationwide" mode, never a default), `lat`/`lon`/`radiusKm` (required when scope=nearby; radiusKm defaults to 5, max 25).

On connect, sends the current snapshot as a burst of `location` events, then streams live updates. Event types:
- `location`: a `VehicleLocation` — a vehicle moved.
- `offline`: `{"vehicleId": <int>}` — a vehicle's driving session ended; the client should remove its pin immediately rather than waiting for it to go stale.
- `reconnect`: no data — sent shortly before the access token expires, so the client reconnects with a fresh one.
- `error`: an `ErrorResponse` — sent once and the stream ends, if `scope`/`lat`/`lon`/`radiusKm` failed validation.

post.description: Buyer-only. Signals "I'd like to buy something" to whoever's currently driving. Rate-limited by a per-(buyer, vehicle) cooldown (409/429-shaped as COOLDOWN_ACTIVE) independent of the standard API rate limit. The buyer's location is privacy-coarsened to an H3 cell center before it's stored or delivered anywhere — the exact coordinate never persists.

202.description: Delivered (live via SSE if the driver's connected, and via push either way)

409.description: Vehicle has no active driving session right now

429.description: Cooldown active for this (buyer, vehicle) pair

get.summary: Live pings for the driving vendor (SSE)
get.description: Server-Sent Events stream. Vendor-only. Streams `ping` events (a `VehiclePingNotification`) as buyers ping whichever vehicle the caller is currently driving. Also emits `reconnect` (no data) shortly before token expiry. A ping while the vendor isn't connected here is still delivered via push notification separately — this stream is the real-time-while-open complement, not the only delivery path.

post.summary: Register a device for push notifications
post.description: Any authenticated user. Re-registering the same installation id is a clean upsert, not an error. `installationId` is a Firebase Installation ID (FID), not a legacy FCM registration token.

delete.description: Only the owning user can remove their own installation.

post.description: The geofence source for proximity notifications about favorited companies' vehicles. Idempotent by (caller, request body).

delete.description: Only the owning user can delete their own — deleting someone else's returns not-found, never a permission-leak.

get.description: Multi-device sync outbox (ADR 0006) for the caller's own low-frequency CRUD entities (companies, vehicles, vehicle assignments, memberships, favorites, saved locations) — never high-frequency GPS telemetry, which is exempt by design.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Cursor (event id) to pull changes after; defaults to 0

get.description: Server-Sent Events stream. Emits a `changed` event (data: the sync event id) as a hint to re-pull via `GET /api/v1/sync` — never the changed data itself. Skips hints for the connecting device's own actions. Also emits `reconnect` (no data) shortly before token expiry. Backed by Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY, so this works across multiple backend instances without needing Redis.
